text.ms:
1. (1) Peraturan-peraturan ini bolehlah dinamakan Peraturan-Peraturan

Kawalan Dadah dan Kosmetik (Pindaan) 2013.

(2) Peraturan-Peraturan ini mula berkuat kuasa pada 28 Mac 2013.

Pindaan subperaturan 7(1A)

2. Peraturan-Peraturan Kawalan Dadah dan Kosmetik 1984 [P.U. (A) 223/1984],

yang disebut "Peraturan-Peraturan ibu" dalam Peraturan-Peraturan ini, dipinda dalam

subperaturan 7(1A) dengan memasukkan selepas perenggan (g), perenggan berikut:

"(h) yang mengandungi bahan cemaran logam melainkan jika terjadi secara

semula jadi, yang terdapat di dalam mana-mana ubat tradisional sebagaimana

yang dinyatakan dalam ruang (1) Daftar I kepada Jadual, dalam kadar yang tidak

melebihi kadar maksimum yang dibenarkan yang dinyatakan bersetentangan

dengan bahan itu dalam ruang (2) Daftar itu.".

Peraturan baru 7A

3. Peraturan-Peraturan ibu dipinda dengan memasukkan selepas peraturan 7,

peraturan yang berikut:

SALE OF DRUGS ACT 1952

CONTROL OF DRUGS AND COSMETICS (AMENDMENT) REGULATIONS 2013

IN exercise of the powers conferred by subsection 26(1) of the Sale of Drugs Act 1952

[Act 368], the Minister makes the following regulations:

Citation and commencement

1. (1) These regulations may be cited as the Control of Drugs and

Cosmetics (Amendment) Regulations 2013.

(2) These Regulations come into operation on 28 March 2013.

Amendment of subregulation 7(1A)

2. The Control of Drugs and Cosmetics Regulations 1984 [P.U. (A) 223/1984], which

are referred to as the "principal Regulations" in these Regulations, are amended in

subregulation 7(1A) by inserting after paragraph (g) the following paragraph:

"(h) which contains any metal contaminant unless naturally occurs, which

contained in any traditional medicine as specified in column (1) of Table I to the

Schedule in a proportion not greater than the maximum permitted proportion

specified opposite the substance in column (2) of the Table.".

New regulation

3. The principal Regulations are amended by inserting after regulation 7, the

following regulation:

7A. No person shall manufacture, sell, supply, import, possess or

administer any traditional medicine which contains any substance

as set out in Table II to the Schedule.".

Amendment of Schedule

4. The Schedule of the principal Regulations is amended by inserting after Form 5,

the following tables:

"TABLE I

(Regulation 7)

MAXIMUM PERMITTED PROPORTION OF NATURALLY OCCURRING METAL

CONTAMINANT IN TRADITIONAL MEDICINE

(1)

Substance

(Metal Contaminant)

(2)

Maximum permitted proportion

Arsenic 5.0 mg/kg or 5.0 mg/litre or 5.0 ppm

Cadmium 0.3 mg/kg or 0.3 mg/litre or 0.3 ppm

Lead 10.0mg/kg or 10.0 mg/litre or 10.0 ppm

Mercury 0.5 mg/kg or 0.5 mg/litre or 0.5 ppm

TABLE II

(Regulation 7A)

PROHIBITED SUBSTANCES IN TRADITIONAL MEDICINE

The following substances are prohibited in traditional medicine:

1. Caffeine

2. Nicotinamide

3. Paracetamol

4. Poison within the meaning of the Poisons Act 1952 [Act 366]".

Made 11 March 2013

[KK(R) 608(13/2)Bhg. ; PN(PU2)269A/IV]

DATO' SRI LIOW TIONG LAI

Minister of Health
